quizzes.title: India's Arms Import Sources
quizzes.passage: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, known as SIPRI, is an independent international research institute. It has its headquarters in Stockholm, Sweden. Its focus areas include conflict and peace studies, armaments and military expenditure, arms transfers and disarmament. The institute released a report titled Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025, which analyses global defence trade patterns. The report covers international arms transfers during the 2021-25 period and compares them with the 2016-20 period. Among its key global findings, international arms transfers increased over the comparison period, while arms imports by European countries rose sharply, a rise the report largely links to the Russia-Ukraine war. The report also records that arms exports from Russia declined, reducing its share of global exports. The United States is shown as the top exporter, followed by France, Russia, Germany and China. The findings are presented as a set of key global findings, followed by specific findings for India. India is discussed as one of the major importers in the report, and its arms imports are examined for the 2021-25 period. The analysis covers the countries that supply India and the trends in its overall import volumes. Taken together, the report provides a broad view of how weapons move between countries, and it places India within this wider pattern of global defence trade.

questions.q: What share of India's arms imports during 2021-25 came from Russia?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Russia supplied 40% of India's arms imports during 2021-25.

questions.q: What percentage of India's arms imports during 2021-25 came from France?
questions.explanation: France accounted for 29% of India's arms imports during 2021-25, according to the booklet.

questions.q: Which country supplied 15% of India's arms imports during 2021-25?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Israel as supplying 15% of India's arms imports during 2021-25.

questions.q: Which factor is linked to the decline in India's overall arms imports during 2021-25?
options: A shift in diplomatic relations with Russia
Increased domestic defence manufacturing and indigenisation
questions.explanation: The booklet attributes the decline mainly to increased domestic defence manufacturing and indigenisation.

questions.q:
Read the following statements.
Assertion (A): Israel was among the three main suppliers of India's arms imports during 2021-25.
Reason (R): Israel accounted for 29% of India's arms imports during 2021-25.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Israel's share was 15%, not 29% (which was France's share), so R is false while A is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's arms imports during 2021-25.
I. Increased domestic manufacturing and indigenisation efforts are linked to the decline in overall imports.
II. Russia accounted for 29% of India's arms imports.
III. Israel accounted for 15% of India's arms imports.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II wrongly gives Russia's share as France's 29%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's arms imports during 2021-25.
I. France accounted for 29% of India's arms imports.
II. Russia accounted for 15% of India's arms imports.
III. Israel accounted for 29% of India's arms imports.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Russia's share was 40% and Israel's was 15%.

quizzes.title: India's Defence Self-Reliance Push
quizzes.passage: India has several government initiatives in its defence sector, which the report describes under the heading of efforts to reduce arms imports. The government has announced a defence budget for the 2026-27 year, and the report records the value of defence production and exports for the year 2024-25. Targets have also been set for production and exports for the year 2029. Policy steps are aimed at building a domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem, and special industrial zones are being developed to support this aim. The rules for foreign investment in defence are structured in two parts, one for investment through the automatic route and another through the government route. Innovation in the sector is also an area of focus under the government programmes. The top three destinations for Indian defence exports are named in the report. The report sets out these figures as part of the country efforts to build its defence capacity, and the initiatives are presented together so that production, exports, investment and innovation can be read as one set of measures. Together, these measures show how the country is trying to expand its own capacity to produce defence equipment while reducing its reliance on arms bought from other countries.

questions.q: What is India's defence production target for 2029?
questions.explanation: The booklet sets the 2029 defence production target at Rs 3 lakh crore.

questions.q: What was the value of India's defence exports in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The booklet records defence exports in 2024-25 as Rs 23,622 crore.

questions.q: Under the government route, up to what percentage of FDI is permitted in India's defence sector?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that 100% FDI is permitted through the government route.

questions.q:
Read the following statements.
Assertion (A): Under the Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020, Indian-made products are prioritised over foreign purchases.
Reason (R): Defence Industrial Corridors have been established in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the corridors do not explain the procurement priority.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. iDEX   ->   A. Innovation support for startups and MSMEs
II. Defence Industrial Corridors   ->   B. Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
III. Top three export destinations   ->   C. US, France and Armenia
IV. Defence budget 2026-27   ->   D. Rs 7.85 lakh crore
questions.explanation: Each item in List I matches its counterpart in List II as stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's defence sector.
I. iDEX supports startups and MSMEs in defence innovation.
II. The government route permits FDI of up to 74%.
III. Armenia is among the top three defence export destinations.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while II wrongly gives the automatic route's 74% limit as the government route's limit.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's defence sector.
I. The Defence Industrial Corridors are located in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
II. The automatic route FDI limit in defence is 49%.
III. iDEX stands for Innovations for Defence Excellence.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong since the automatic route permits 74%.
